html:
Omar Torrijos was a Panamanian army officer who led the government of Panama from 1968 until 1981. He negotiated the treaties that returned the Panama Canal to Panama.

He took power in a coup against the elected president Arnulfo Arias in 1968. He ruled as an authoritarian populist, building schools, roads and clinics, giving land to peasants and passing a labour code, while his opponents were silenced. His intelligence chief was Manuel Noriega.

His great cause was the canal. He won world support at the United Nations and in 1977 signed the Torrijos-Carter treaties with President Jimmy Carter. He died in a plane crash in 1981. He is still a hero to many in Panama, and his son Martín was later president. The novelist García Márquez was his friend.
sum: Omar Torrijos was a Panamanian army officer who led the government of Panama from 1968 until 1981. He negotiated the treaties that returned the Panama Canal to Panama.
